output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: LoggerRequestProcessor.process() takes a raw `path` string straight out of untrusted Netty command payloads (ViewLogRequestCommand, GetLogBytesRequestCommand, RollViewLogRequestCommand, RemoveTaskLogRequestCommand) and passes it directly into File/FileInputStream/Files.lines with no validation, so a caller who can reach the log-server port (default 50051) can supply '../' sequences or absolute paths to read or delete arbitrary files on the host.

Fix (trust-boundary check at the single dispatch point in LoggerRequestProcessor.process, so it covers all sink call sites uniformly):
1. Added LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() (dolphinscheduler-server LogUtils) which resolves the configured task log root directory from the logback TASKLOGFILE appender's TaskLogDiscriminator, returning it as a normalized absolute path.
2. Added a private helper LoggerRequestProcessor.isLogPathIllegal(String filePath) that: rejects blank paths, rejects when the log base path itself cannot be determined (fail closed), and otherwise resolves+normalizes both the log base and the requested path with java.nio.file.Path and checks target.startsWith(base). This normalizes '..' segments, symlinked/relative segments, and mixed absolute/relative forms, so all the traversal styles in the report (and same-class bypass variants) are blocked by one check.
3. Applied the check before the sink in all four switch cases (GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST, ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST, and REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST — the last one added defense-in-depth since it's a sibling call site in the same untrusted dispatch switch with the same unvalidated-path pattern, doing a file delete instead of a read). On rejection the handlers return an empty/false result and log a warning instead of touching the filesystem, preserving existing response shapes and not breaking normal (in-root) log viewing/downloading/paging/removal.

Regression tests added to LoggerRequestProcessorTest: legitimate path inside the log root still returns file content; a '../' traversal path for VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST, GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST, and ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST is denied (empty response, verified via captured outbound Command), each using a real temp directory + real secret file, with LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() mocked to point at the temp log root (PowerMock static mocking, consistent with the existing LogUtilsTest pattern used for the same logback appender chain).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only tightens an existing unauthenticated internal RPC surface (the log server) by rejecting requests whose path resolves outside the configured log directory; it does not alter behavior for any path that already resolved under the log root, which is how all legitimate callers (API/master/worker requesting task logs by constructed path) operate. One assumption: LogUtils.getTaskLogBasePath() must be able to resolve the TASKLOGFILE logback appender/discriminator at runtime (it already backs the pre-existing LogUtils.getTaskLogPath() used elsewhere) — if logging config is ever customized to omit that appender, all log requests will be fail-closed (denied) rather than silently permissive, which is the safe direction for this trust boundary. Did not modify dolphinscheduler-common/LoggerUtils.java (readWholeFileContent) itself, since it is a low-level generic file reader also usable safely once the caller-side check is in place; validating at the single Netty command dispatch point (LoggerRequestProcessor) covers every current sink and is easier to review/maintain than duplicating checks in each low-level utility.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in the DolphinScheduler log server (LoggerRequestProcessor) by confining all externally supplied log paths (from VIEW_WHOLE_LOG_REQUEST, GET_LOG_BYTES_REQUEST, ROLL_VIEW_LOG_REQUEST, and REMOVE_TAK_LOG_REQUEST Netty commands) to the configured task log root directory before any file I/O is performed.
